summary: Michael Oppitz works in Tibetology and other fields. He held posts at the Wissenschaftskolleg zu Berlin (circa 1987–1988) and the University of Zurich, where he served as Leiter (circa 1999–2008).
Michael P. Berman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. Attested in 2012, he served as a professor at Brock University and as managing editor of the Canadian Journal of Buddhist Studies.

Michael Puett specializes in Sinology, history and archaeology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (circa 1987–1994) under Marshall Sahlins and Anthony C. Yu, later holding professorships at Harvard University from circa 2001.

Michael Pye works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Cambridge and Leeds under Maurice Wiles, and held teaching posts at Leeds (circa 1968–1984), Lancaster (1991–1994), and the University of Marburg (1982–2004).

Michael Radich specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at Harvard (circa 2001–2007) under Robert M. Gimello and Michael Puett, later holding posts at Victoria University of Wellington (2005–2017) and Heidelberg University (2018).
Michael S. Drummond is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed an MA in Buddhist Studies at the University of Bristol and was a PhD candidate at Utrecht University (attested 2006).

Michael Schmidt is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (1979, 1992, attested 2008), the Katalogisierung der orientalischen Handschriften in Deutschland (1992), and the University of Göttingen (attested 1995).

Michael Sheehy works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies under Steven D. Goodman (attested 2007) and has held posts at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center and the University of Virginia.
Michael Silverstein was a linguist who studied at Stuyvesant High School and Harvard University (circa 1962–1971). He held an academic post at the University of Chicago from circa 1970 to 2020.

Michael Stanley-Baker works in Sinology and religious studies. He earned an MA at Indiana University Bloomington under Stephen R. Bokenkamp, and has held posts at the Max Planck Institute, the University of Leipzig, Nanyang Technological University, and the University of Pittsburgh.
Michael Torsten Much is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Ernst Steinkellner and was a fellow at the University of Hamburg.

Michael Viggo Fausbøll was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Copenhagen (1838–1847) under Niels Ludvig Westergaard. He served at the University of Copenhagen as sub-librarian (1861) and as professor of Indian philology (1878–1902).

Michael W. Meister specializes in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at Harvard University (BA, MA, PhD) and the University of Pennsylvania, where he became a professor in 1976, succeeding Stella Kramrisch.

Michael Weiers is a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Bonn (circa 1959–1965), where he served as professor from 1972 to 2003, and was an honorary professor at Inner Mongolia University.

Michael Wenger is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned an MA at The New School, studied under Mel Weitsman, served as Dean of Buddhist Studies at the San Francisco Zen Center (circa 1984–2012), and founded Dragons Leap Meditation Center.

Michael Willis works in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Victoria and earned a doctorate from the University of Chicago, later teaching at SUNY New Paltz and serving as curator at the British Museum (1994–2014).

Michael Witzel specializes in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Karl Hoffmann and Paul Thieme, among others, and held posts as leader of the Nepal Research Centre (1972–1978), Chair of Sanskrit at Leiden (1978–1986), and Sanskrit professor at Harvard (from 1986).

Michael Zimmermann works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg (circa 1993–2000) under Lambert Schmithausen and held posts at Stanford University (2003) and the University of Hamburg (circa 2007).

Michael von Brück works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed his promotion at the University of Rostock and held professorships in comparative religion and religious studies at the University of Regensburg (1988–1991) and the University of Munich (circa 1991–2014).

Michaela Haas is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Bonn (attested 2008) under Peter Schwieger and studied under Jigme Namgyal Dzigar Kongtrul and Rechungpa.
